_CONTROL_CHARS = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]")


class JsonLogFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        payload: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime(record.created))
                  + f".{int(record.msecs):03d}Z",

            "logger": record.name,
            "event": record.getMessage(),

            payload.update(extra)
        if record.exc_info:

        return json.dumps(payload, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)

                 retry_after: Optional[int] = None,
                 log_level: int = logging.WARNING) -> None:

        self.message = message
        self.details = details or {}

# Accepted image types + magic-byte sniffing

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ImageType:
    key: str
    mime: str
    ext: str
    pillow_format: str


JPEG = ImageType("jpeg", "image/jpeg", "jpg", "JPEG")
PNG = ImageType("png", "image/png", "png", "PNG")
GIF = ImageType("gif", "image/gif", "gif", "GIF")
WEBP = ImageType("webp", "image/webp", "webp", "WEBP")

ALLOWED_TYPES: Tuple[ImageType, ...] = (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP)
_EXT_TO_TYPE = {"jpg": JPEG, "jpeg": JPEG, "jpe": JPEG, "jfif": JPEG,
                "png": PNG, "gif": GIF, "webp": WEBP}


def sniff_image_type(head: bytes) -> Optional[ImageType]:
    """
    FM-10: identify format from magic bytes ONLY. The Content-Type header and the
    filename extension are untrusted hints, never evidence.
    """
    if len(head) < 12:
        return None
    if head[:3] == b"\xff\xd8\xff":                 # JPEG SOI + marker
        return JPEG
    if head[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n":            # PNG signature
        return PNG
    if head[:6] in (b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a"):
        return GIF
    if head[:4] == b"RIFF" and head[8:12] == b"WEBP":
        return WEBP
    return None


# FM-13: markers of content a browser or misconfigured server might execute.
# A GIF/HTML or JPEG/PHP polyglot passes magic-byte sniffing, so scan the head.
# Scanned window is deliberately small (SCAN_SIZE) to avoid false positives on
# legitimate XMP/EXIF metadata blocks further into the file.
_DANGEROUS_MARKERS: Tuple[bytes, ...] = (
    b"<?php", b"<script", b"<html", b"<!doctype html", b"<iframe",
    b"javascript:", b"#!/bin/", b"#!/usr/bin/", b"\x7felf", b"pk\x03\x04",
)


def scan_for_dangerous_content(head: bytes) -> Optional[str]:
    if not CFG.SCAN_EMBEDDED_SCRIPTS:
        return None
    lowered = head[: CFG.SCAN_SIZE].lower()
    for marker in _DANGEROUS_MARKERS:
        if marker in lowered:
            return marker.decode("latin-1", "replace")
    return None


def check_structural_integrity(head: bytes, tail: bytes, total: int,
                               itype: ImageType) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    FM-14: reject appended payloads. The classic attack glues a ZIP/PHAR/PHP blob
    after a valid image's terminator; every format below has a definite end marker.
    """
    if itype is JPEG:
        if tail[-2:] != b"\xff\xd9":                      # EOI must be final
            return "jpeg_trailing_data_after_eoi"
    elif itype is PNG:
        if len(tail) < 8 or tail[-8:-4] != b"IEND":       # IEND + CRC must be final
            return "png_trailing_data_after_iend"
    elif itype is GIF:
        if tail[-1:] != b"\x3b":                          # GIF trailer
            return "gif_trailing_data_after_trailer"
    elif itype is WEBP:
        declared = int.from_bytes(head[4:8], "little") + 8
        if declared != total:      # RIFF declares its own length
            return f"webp_riff_size_mismatch(declared={declared},actual={total})"
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filename sanitization
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_RESERVED_NAMES = {
    "con", "prn", "aux", "nul",
    *(f"com{i}" for i in range(1, 10)),
    *(f"lpt{i}" for i in range(1, 10)),
}
# Bidi/format controls used to visually reverse an extension:
# "evil\u202Etxt.exe" renders as "evilexe.txt".
_BIDI_AND_FORMAT = re.compile(
    "[\u200b-\u200f\u202a-\u202e\u2060-\u2064\u2066-\u2069\ufeff]"
)
_UNSAFE_CHARS = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]")
_REPEATED_UNDERSCORE = re.compile(r"_{2,}")
_LEADING_JUNK = re.compile(r"^[._-]+")


def sanitize_filename(raw: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
    """
    Returns (safe_display_name, applied_transform_flags).

    NOTE: this name is used for display/metadata ONLY. The on-disk path derives
    from the content hash (build_final_path), so even total failure of this
    function cannot produce a path-traversal write. Defense in depth, not the
    sole defense.
    """
    flags: List[str] = []
    if not raw:
        return "upload", ["empty_filename"]

    name = raw
    # FM-30: embedded NUL truncates paths in C-level APIs ("shell.php\x00.jpg").
    if "\x00" in name:
        flags.append("null_byte")
        name = name.split("\x00", 1)[0]

    # FM-31: unicode normalization — fullwidth "．／" otherwise survives filtering.
    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", name)
    if normalized != name:
        flags.append("nfkc_normalized")
        name = normalized

    # FM-32: bidi override / zero-width extension spoofing.
    stripped = _BIDI_AND_FORMAT.sub("", name)
    if stripped != name:
        flags.append("bidi_controls_removed")
        name = stripped

    # FM-33: control characters and newlines (also a log-injection vector).
    cleaned = _CONTROL_CHARS.sub("", name)
    if cleaned != name:
        flags.append("control_chars_removed")
        name = cleaned

    # FM-34: path traversal in every dialect — POSIX, Windows, drive-relative, UNC.
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
        flags.append("path_components_stripped")
        name = re.split(r"[\\/]", name)[-1]
    # FM-35: NTFS Alternate Data Streams ("file.jpg:payload.exe") and "C:evil.jpg".
    if ":" in name:
        flags.append("drive_or_ads_stripped")
        name = name.split(":")[-1] or name.split(":")[0]

    if name.strip(".") == "":            # "." / ".." / "..." as the whole name
        flags.append("dot_only_name")
        name = "upload"

    # FM-36: chars legal on disk but hostile in shells, URLs and HTML.
    substituted = _UNSAFE_CHARS.sub("_", name)
    if substituted != name:
        flags.append("unsafe_chars_replaced")
        name = substituted
    name = _REPEATED_UNDERSCORE.sub("_", name)

    # FM-37: leading dot = hidden file; leading dash = parsed as a CLI flag.
    delead = _LEADING_JUNK.sub("", name)
    if delead != name:
        flags.append("leading_junk_stripped")
        name = delead

    # FM-38: Windows silently strips trailing dots/spaces, so "x.php ." can
    # resolve back to "x.php" after transfer.
    detrail = name.rstrip(". ")
    if detrail != name:
        flags.append("trailing_dots_stripped")
        name = detrail

    if not name:
        return "upload", flags + ["empty_after_sanitize"]

    # FM-39: reserved device names, with or without an extension.
    if name.split(".", 1)[0].lower() in _RESERVED_NAMES:
        flags.append("reserved_name")
        name = f"file_{name}"

    # FM-40: overlong names blow past NAME_MAX (255 bytes).
    if len(name) > CFG.MAX_FILENAME_CHARS:
        flags.append("truncated")
        base, dot, ext = name.rpartition(".")
        if dot and 0 < len(ext) <= 8:
            name = f"{base[:CFG.MAX_FILENAME_CHARS - len(ext) - 1]}.{ext}"
        else:
            name = name[: CFG.MAX_FILENAME_CHARS]

    # FM-41: double extensions ("invoice.php.jpg") — flagged, not rejected, since
    # the stored path never uses this name and legitimate files do contain dots.
    if len([p for p in name.split(".") if p]) > 2:
        flags.append("multiple_extensions")

    return name, flags


def extension_of(name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    base, dot, ext = name.rpartition(".")
    if not dot or not base:
        return None
    ext = ext.lower()
    return ext if 0 < len(ext) <= 8 else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rate limiting + admission control
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TokenBucketLimiter:
    """
    FM-60: per-client request-rate cap. In-process only — behind multiple workers
    this limits per worker; the authoritative limiter belongs in Redis or the edge.
    """

    def __init__(self, burst: int, per_minute: int, max_tracked: int) -> None:
        self._burst = float(burst)
        self._rate = per_minute / 60.0
        self._max_tracked = max_tracked
        self._buckets: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]] = {}
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def acquire(self, key: str) -> Tuple[bool, int]:
        now = time.monotonic()
        async with self._lock:
            # FM-61: unbounded key growth is itself a memory-exhaustion DoS.
            if len(self._buckets) > self._max_tracked:
                cutoff = now - 300
                self._buckets = {k: v for k, v in self._buckets.items()
                                 if v[1] > cutoff}
                if len(self._buckets) > self._max_tracked:
                    self._buckets.clear()

            tokens, last = self._buckets.get(key, (self._burst, now))
            tokens = min(self._burst, tokens + (now - last) * self._rate)
            if tokens < 1.0:
                self._buckets[key] = (tokens, now)
                return False, max(1, int((1.0 - tokens) / self._rate) + 1)
            self._buckets[key] = (tokens - 1.0, now)
            return True, 0


class PerClientConcurrency:
    """FM-62: one client must not be able to occupy every upload slot."""

    def __init__(self, limit: int) -> None:
        self._limit = limit
        self._counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def slot(self, key: str):
        async with self._lock:
            current = self._counts.get(key, 0)
            if current >= self._limit:
                raise UploadError(
                    "TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS", 429,
                    "Too many concurrent uploads from this client.",
                    details={"limit": self._limit}, retry_after=5,
                )
            self._counts[key] = current + 1
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            async with self._lock:   # FM-63: counter map must not leak keys
                remaining = self._counts.get(key, 1) - 1
                if remaining <= 0:
                    self._counts.pop(key, None)
                else:
                    self._counts[key] = remaining


class IdempotencyCache:
    """
    FM-70: a client retrying after a dropped response must not create a second
    object. Keyed by Idempotency-Key, scoped per client identity.
    """

    def __init__(self, ttl: int, max_entries: int) -> None:
        self._ttl = ttl
        self._max = max_entries
        self._entries: Dict[str, Tuple[float, Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def get(self, key: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        async with self._lock:
            entry = self._entries.get(key)
            if entry is None:
                return None
            expires, payload = entry
            if expires < time.monotonic():
                self._entries.pop(key, None)
                return None
            return payload

    async def put(self, key: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        async with self._lock:
            if len(self._entries) >= self._max:
                now = time.monotonic()
                self._entries = {k: v for k, v in self._entries.items() if v[0] > now}
                for k in sorted(self._entries,
                                key=lambda k: self._entries[k][0])[: self._max // 2]:
                    self._entries.pop(k, None)
            self._entries[key] = (time.monotonic() + self._ttl, payload)

# Storage layer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class StoredFile:
    sha256: str
    size: int
    relative_path: str

def _ensure_directory(path: str) -> None:
    os.makedirs(path, mode=CFG.DIR_MODE, exist_ok=True)


def prepare_storage() -> None:
    """Startup validation — fail loudly at boot, not on the first upload."""
    temp_dir = os.path.join(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT, CFG.TEMP_DIRNAME)
    try:
        _ensure_directory(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT)
        _ensure_directory(temp_dir)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"cannot create storage root {CFG.STORAGE_ROOT}: {exc}")

    # FM-21: the account must actually be able to WRITE, not merely traverse.
    probe = os.path.join(temp_dir, f".probe-{uuid.uuid4().hex}")
    try:
        fd = os.open(probe, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
        os.write(fd, b"ok")
        os.close(fd)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"storage root is not writable: {exc}")
    finally:
        with suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(probe)

    # FM-22: os.replace() is atomic only WITHIN a filesystem. If the temp dir is a
    # separate mount, every upload would fail with EXDEV at the final step — catch
    # that at boot rather than in production traffic.
    if os.stat(temp_dir).st_dev != os.stat(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT).st_dev:
        raise SystemExit("temp dir and storage root are on different filesystems")

    if CFG.REQUIRE_DEEP_VALIDATION and not PILLOW_AVAILABLE:
        raise SystemExit("Pillow is required for deep image validation")


def check_free_space(expected: int) -> None:
    """
    FM-23: refuse early when the disk is nearly full. Advisory only — the write
    loop remains authoritative, because free space can vanish between check and
    write (TOCTOU).
    """
    try:
        usage = os.statvfs(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT)
        free = usage.f_bavail * usage.f_frsize
    except (OSError, AttributeError):
        return
    if free < expected + CFG.FREE_SPACE_HEADROOM:
        raise UploadError("STORAGE_FULL", 507, "Insufficient storage available.",
                          details={"free_bytes": free}, retry_after=30,
                          log_level=logging.ERROR)


def build_final_path(digest: str, itype: ImageType) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """
    Content-addressed, sharded layout: <root>/ab/cd/<sha256>.<ext>

    FM-42: the stored name derives entirely from the content hash and the SNIFFED
    type. No byte of client input reaches the path — traversal, collision-overwrite
    and extension-confusion are foreclosed by construction.
    FM-24: two-level sharding keeps directory entry counts sane; millions of files
    in one directory degrades badly on ext4/NFS.
    """
    relative = os.path.join(digest[:2], digest[2:4], f"{digest}.{itype.ext}")
    absolute = os.path.join(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT, relative)

    # FM-43: containment assertion. If this function is ever refactored to include
    # user input, the write stops here instead of trusting the refactor.
    real_root = os.path.realpath(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT)
    real_target = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(absolute))
    if os.path.commonpath([real_root, real_target]) != real_root:
        raise UploadError("PATH_ESCAPE_DETECTED", 500,
                          "Refusing to write outside storage root.",
                          log_level=logging.ERROR)
    return absolute, relative


def write_all(fd: int, chunk: bytes) -> None:
    """
    FM-25: os.write() may write FEWER bytes than requested (signals, quota edges,
    slow devices). Silently accepting a short write is how files get truncated.
    """
    view = memoryview(chunk)
    while view:
        written = os.write(fd, view)
        if written <= 0:
            raise OSError(errno.EIO, "zero-length write")
        view = view[written:]


def finalize_temp_file(fd: int) -> None:
    """FM-26: durability. Without fsync a power loss can leave a 0-length file."""
    if CFG.FSYNC:
        os.fsync(fd)
    os.fchmod(fd, CFG.FILE_MODE)


def _fsync_path(path: str) -> None:
    if not CFG.FSYNC:
        return
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def atomic_publish(temp_path: str, final_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    FM-27: the atomic-rename dance. Returns True if the object already existed.

    os.replace() is atomic within a filesystem, and rename(2) does NOT follow a
    symlink at the destination — it replaces the link itself — so a planted
    symlink cannot redirect the write outside the root.
    """
    directory = os.path.dirname(final_path)
    try:
        _ensure_directory(directory)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise storage_error(exc, "mkdir")

    # FM-71: content-addressed dedup — identical bytes are already stored.
    already = os.path.exists(final_path)

    try:
        os.replace(temp_path, final_path)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise storage_error(exc, "rename")

    # FM-28: fsync the DIRECTORY, not just the file. The rename is metadata and is
    # not durable until the containing directory is synced.
    if CFG.FSYNC:
        with suppress(OSError):   # some filesystems reject dir fsync; not fatal
            _fsync_path(directory)
    return already


def sweep_stale_temp_files(max_age: int) -> int:
    """
    FM-80: a process killed mid-upload leaves a temp file forever. Sweep at startup
    and periodically so a crash loop cannot fill the disk with orphans.
    """
    temp_dir = os.path.join(CFG.STORAGE_ROOT, CFG.TEMP_DIRNAME)
    removed = 0
    now = time.time()
    try:
        entries = os.scandir(temp_dir)
    except OSError:
        return 0
    with entries:
        for entry in entries:
            try:
                if not entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False):
                    continue
                if now - entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mtime > max_age:
                    os.unlink(entry.path)
                    removed += 1
            except OSError:
                continue   # racing with another worker's cleanup is fine
    return removed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deep image validation (Pillow) — runs in a worker thread
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class ImageMetadata:
    width: int
    height: int
    frames: int
    mode: str
    has_exif: bool = False


def validate_image_sync(path: str, expected: ImageType) -> ImageMetadata:
    """
    Magic bytes only prove the first few bytes. This pass proves the file actually
    DECODES — which is what a downstream thumbnailer or browser will attempt.
    """
    if not PILLOW_AVAILABLE:
        return ImageMetadata(0, 0, 1, "unknown")

    # FM-15: decompression bomb. A 4 KB PNG can declare 60000x60000 and demand
    # ~10 GB of RAM on decode. Pillow raises DecompressionBombError above this.
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = CFG.MAX_PIXELS
    # FM-16: never silently accept truncated image data.
    ImageFile.LOAD_TRUNCATED_IMAGES = False

    try:
        with Image.open(path) as img:
            # FM-17: container magic and Pillow's decoder must AGREE. Disagreement
            # means a crafted hybrid file.
            if img.format != expected.pillow_format:
                raise UploadError(
                    "FORMAT_MISMATCH", 415,
                    "File content does not match its detected image format.",
                    details={"sniffed": expected.mime, "decoded": img.format},
                )
            width, height = img.size
            mode = img.mode
            frames = int(getattr(img, "n_frames", 1) or 1)
            has_exif = bool(img.info.get("exif"))

            # FM-18: degenerate or absurd dimensions break every consumer.
            if width < CFG.MIN_DIMENSION or height < CFG.MIN_DIMENSION:
                raise UploadError("IMAGE_TOO_SMALL", 400,
                                  "Image dimensions are invalid.",
                                  details={"width": width, "height": height})
            if width > CFG.MAX_DIMENSION or height > CFG.MAX_DIMENSION:
                raise UploadError("IMAGE_DIMENSIONS_TOO_LARGE", 400,
                                  f"Image exceeds {CFG.MAX_DIMENSION}px on a side.",
                                  details={"width": width, "height": height})
            if width * height > CFG.MAX_PIXELS:
                raise UploadError("IMAGE_TOO_MANY_PIXELS", 400,
                                  "Image has too many pixels.",
                                  details={"pixels": width * height,
                                           "limit": CFG.MAX_PIXELS})
            # FM-19: a GIF/WebP with 100k frames is a CPU bomb at any resolution.
            if frames > CFG.MAX_FRAMES:
                raise UploadError("IMAGE_TOO_MANY_FRAMES", 400,
                                  "Animated image has too many frames.",
                                  details={"frames": frames,
                                           "limit": CFG.MAX_FRAMES})
            img.verify()   # CRC/structural check; consumes the instance

        # verify() leaves the object unusable, so reopen and force a REAL decode.
        # This is what actually catches truncated scan data and corrupt DCT blocks.
        with Image.open(path) as img2:
            img2.load()

        return ImageMetadata(width, height, frames, mode, has_exif)

    except UploadError:
        raise
    except UnidentifiedImageError:
        raise UploadError("IMAGE_UNREADABLE", 415, "File is not a readable image.")
    except Exception as exc:   # DecompressionBombError, OSError("truncated"), ...
        name = type(exc).__name__
        if "DecompressionBomb" in name:
            raise UploadError("IMAGE_DECOMPRESSION_BOMB", 400,
                              "Image is too large to decode safely.")
        raise UploadError("IMAGE_CORRUPT", 400,
                          "Image data is corrupt or truncated.",
                          details={"reason": name})


def strip_metadata_sync(path: str, itype: ImageType,
                        meta: ImageMetadata) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    FM-50: EXIF carries GPS coordinates, device serials, and embedded thumbnails
    that can differ from the visible image. Opt-in because re-encoding is lossy.
    Returns a new temp path, or None if stripping was skipped.
    """
    if not PILLOW_AVAILABLE or not CFG.STRIP_METADATA:
        return None
    if itype not in (JPEG, PNG) or meta.frames > 1:
        return None   # animation would be lost; trailing-data checks cover these

    out_path = f"{path}.stripped"
    try:
        with Image.open(path) as img:
            clean = Image.new(img.mode, img.size)
            clean.putdata(list(img.getdata()))   # drops all ancillary chunks
            if itype is JPEG:
                clean.save(out_path, format="JPEG", quality=92, optimize=True)
            else:
                clean.save(out_path, format="PNG", optimize=True)
        return out_path
    except Exception:
        with suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(out_path)
        return None

@dataclass
class AppState:
    admission: Any = None
    cpu_limiter: Any = None
    rate_limiter: Any = None
    per_client: Any = None
    idempotency: Any = None
    inflight: int = 0
    shutting_down: bool = False
    reaper_task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None


STATE = AppState()


async def _reaper_loop() -> None:
    while True:
        try:
            await asyncio.sleep(CFG.REAPER_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
            removed = await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(
                sweep_stale_temp_files, CFG.TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS)
            if removed:
                log_event(logging.INFO, "temp_reaper.swept", removed=removed)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            raise
        except Exception:
            # FM-81: a crashing background task must never take the service down.
            log_event(logging.ERROR, "temp_reaper.error", exc_info=True)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    prepare_storage()
    STATE.admission = asyncio.Semaphore(CFG.MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS)
    STATE.cpu_limiter = anyio.CapacityLimiter(CFG.CPU_LIMITER_TOKENS)
    STATE.rate_limiter = TokenBucketLimiter(CFG.RATE_LIMIT_BURST,
                                            CFG.RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE,
                                            CFG.RATE_LIMIT_MAX_TRACKED)
    STATE.per_client = PerClientConcurrency(CFG.MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_CLIENT)
    STATE.idempotency = IdempotencyCache(CFG.IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS,
                                         CFG.IDEMPOTENCY_MAX_ENTRIES)

    orphans = await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(sweep_stale_temp_files,
                                             CFG.TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS)
    log_event(logging.INFO, "startup", storage_root=CFG.STORAGE_ROOT,
              max_bytes=CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, orphans_removed=orphans,
              pillow=PILLOW_AVAILABLE)
    STATE.reaper_task = asyncio.create_task(_reaper_loop())
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        # FM-82: graceful drain. Refuse new work, let in-flight uploads finish
        # their atomic rename, so a deploy never severs a request mid-publish.
        STATE.shutting_down = True
        deadline = time.monotonic() + CFG.DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
        while STATE.inflight > 0 and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        if STATE.reaper_task:
            STATE.reaper_task.cancel()
            with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await STATE.reaper_task
        log_event(logging.INFO, "shutdown", abandoned=STATE.inflight)


app = FastAPI(

    redoc_url=None,

)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASGI middleware: hard cap on raw request body bytes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class BodySizeLimitMiddleware:
    """
    FM-01: Content-Length is a CLAIM, not a fact. It can be absent entirely under
    `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, or it can understate the real body. This wraps
    `receive` and counts actual bytes off the wire, so an attacker streaming 10 GB
    is cut off at the limit regardless of headers — before the multipart parser
    ever gets a chance to spool it.
    """

    def __init__(self, app, max_bytes: int) -> None:
        self.app = app
        self.max_bytes = max_bytes

    async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        received = 0

        async def counting_receive():
            nonlocal received
            message = await receive()
            if message["type"] == "http.request":
                received += len(message.get("body", b""))
                if received > self.max_bytes:
                    raise RequestBodyTooLarge()
            return message

        await self.app(scope, counting_receive, send)


app.add_middleware(BodySizeLimitMiddleware, max_bytes=CFG.MAX_BODY_BYTES)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Response helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SECURITY_HEADERS = {
    # FM-91: stop the browser re-sniffing our content type, and keep upload
    # receipts out of intermediary caches.
    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
    "Cache-Control": "no-store",
    "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
}


def error_response(request_id: str, err: UploadError) -> JSONResponse:
    headers = dict(_SECURITY_HEADERS)
    headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
    if err.retry_after is not None:
        headers["Retry-After"] = str(err.retry_after)
    if err.status_code == 413:
        # FM-02: tell the client to stop rather than leaving a half-uploaded body
        # draining into a handler that has already answered.
        headers["Connection"] = "close"
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=err.status_code,
        headers=headers,
        content={"error": {"code": err.code, "message": err.message,
                           "details": err.details},
                 "request_id": request_id},
    )


def request_id_of(request: Request) -> str:
    raw = request.headers.get("x-request-id", "")
    # FM-92: an inbound request id is client-controlled — accept only a safe shape.
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]{8,64}", raw or ""):
        return raw
    return uuid.uuid4().hex


def client_identity(request: Request) -> str:
    """FM-64: trust X-Forwarded-For only when explicitly deployed behind a proxy."""
    if CFG.TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR:
        xff = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")
        if xff:
            candidate = xff.split(",")[0].strip()
            if candidate and len(candidate) <= 64 \
                    and _CONTROL_CHARS.search(candidate) is None:
                return candidate
    return request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exception handlers — nothing escapes as an unstructured stack trace
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@app.exception_handler(RequestBodyTooLarge)
async def _handle_body_too_large(request: Request, exc: RequestBodyTooLarge):
    rid = request_id_of(request)
    err = UploadError("PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE", 413,
                      f"Request body exceeds the {CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES} byte limit.",
                      details={"max_bytes": CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES})
    log_event(logging.WARNING, "upload.attempt", request_id=rid, outcome="rejected",
              status=413, error_code=err.code, client=client_identity(request))
    return error_response(rid, err)


@app.exception_handler(UploadError)
async def _handle_upload_error(request: Request, exc: UploadError):
    return error_response(request_id_of(request), exc)


@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def _handle_unexpected(request: Request, exc: Exception):
    """
    FM-93: unhandled exceptions must return a GENERIC message. Framework defaults
    leak paths, versions and local variables to the client.
    """
    rid = request_id_of(request)
    log_event(logging.ERROR, "upload.unhandled_exception", request_id=rid,
              exc_type=type(exc).__name__, exc_info=True)
    return error_response(rid, UploadError("INTERNAL_ERROR", 500,
                                           "An unexpected error occurred."))

# The endpoint
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@app.post("/api/upload", status_code=201)
async def upload(request: Request):
    request_id = request_id_of(request)
    client = client_identity(request)
    started = time.monotonic()

    # Everything worth logging accumulates here so `finally` can emit exactly one
    # audit record per attempt, success or failure. FM-100.
    audit: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "request_id": request_id,
        "client": client,
        "user_agent": scrub(request.headers.get("user-agent"), 200),
        "declared_content_length": request.headers.get("content-length"),
    }
    outcome = "error"
    status_code = 500

    try:
        # --- FM-83: refuse new work during shutdown so we drain cleanly --------
        if STATE.shutting_down:
            raise UploadError("SERVER_SHUTTING_DOWN", 503,
                              "Server is shutting down.", retry_after=5)

        # --- FM-03: wrong request content type ---------------------------------
        content_type = (request.headers.get("content-type") or "") \
            .split(";")[0].strip().lower()
        if content_type != "multipart/form-data":
            raise UploadError("UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE", 415,
                              "Request must be multipart/form-data.",
                              details={"received": scrub(content_type, 64) or None})

        # --- FM-04: fail fast on a self-declared oversize / absurd body --------
        declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
        if declared is not None:
            try:
                declared_len = int(declared)
            except ValueError:
                raise UploadError("MALFORMED_CONTENT_LENGTH", 400,
                                  "Invalid Content-Length.")
            if declared_len < 0:
                raise UploadError("MALFORMED_CONTENT_LENGTH", 400,
                                  "Invalid Content-Length.")
            if declared_len > CFG.MAX_BODY_BYTES:
                raise UploadError("PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE", 413,
                                  f"File exceeds the {CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES} byte limit.",
                                  details={"max_bytes": CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES,
                                           "declared": declared_len})
            if declared_len == 0:
                raise UploadError("EMPTY_REQUEST", 400, "Request body is empty.")

        # --- FM-60: rate limit BEFORE doing any real work ----------------------
        allowed, retry_after = await STATE.rate_limiter.acquire(client)
        if not allowed:
            raise UploadError("RATE_LIMITED", 429, "Too many upload requests.",
                              retry_after=retry_after)

        # --- FM-70: replay an earlier answer for a retried request -------------
        idem_key_raw = request.headers.get("idempotency-key")
        idem_key = None
        if idem_key_raw and re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]{8,128}", idem_key_raw):
            idem_key = f"{client}:{idem_key_raw}"
            cached = await STATE.idempotency.get(idem_key)
            if cached is not None:
                outcome, status_code = "idempotent_replay", 200
                audit["sha256"] = cached.get("data", {}).get("sha256")
                return JSONResponse(
                    status_code=200,
                    headers={**_SECURITY_HEADERS, "X-Request-ID": request_id,
                             "Idempotent-Replay": "true"},
                    content=cached)

        async with STATE.per_client.slot(client):
            # --- FM-65: global admission control. Unbounded concurrency exhausts
            # FDs, RAM and disk bandwidth; shed load with 503 instead of collapsing.
            try:
                with anyio.fail_after(CFG.ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS):
                    await STATE.admission.acquire()
            except TimeoutError:
                raise UploadError("SERVER_BUSY", 503,
                                  "Server is at capacity; retry shortly.",
                                  retry_after=5)

            STATE.inflight += 1
            try:
                # --- FM-66: bound total request time. Without this, a slowloris
                # client trickling a byte per second holds a slot indefinitely.
                with anyio.fail_after(CFG.REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
                    result = await _process_upload(request, audit)
            except TimeoutError:
                raise UploadError("UPLOAD_TIMEOUT", 408, "Upload timed out.",
                                  details={"timeout_seconds":
                                           CFG.REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS})
            finally:
                STATE.inflight -= 1
                STATE.admission.release()

        payload = {"data": result, "request_id": request_id}
        if idem_key:
            await STATE.idempotency.put(idem_key, payload)

        outcome = "duplicate" if result["duplicate"] else "created"
        status_code = 200 if result["duplicate"] else 201
        audit["sha256"] = result["sha256"]
        audit["size_bytes"] = result["size_bytes"]

        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status_code,
            headers={**_SECURITY_HEADERS, "X-Request-ID": request_id,
                     "Location": result["url"]},
            content=payload)

    except ClientDisconnect:
        # --- FM-84: the client vanished mid-body. Not a server fault — log it
        # distinctly so it does not pollute the 5xx error rate. 499 is never
        # actually delivered (nobody is listening) but keeps the record unambiguous.
        outcome, status_code = "client_disconnect", 499
        raise UploadError("CLIENT_DISCONNECTED", 499,
                          "Client disconnected during upload.",
                          log_level=logging.INFO)
    except UploadError as err:
        outcome, status_code = "rejected", err.status_code
        audit["error_code"] = err.code
        audit["error_details"] = err.details
        raise
    except MultiPartException as exc:
        # --- FM-05: malformed multipart framing (truncated boundary, bad headers,
        # missing terminator) or a part that blew the parser's own size ceiling.
        outcome = "rejected"
        message = str(exc).lower()
        if "exceed" in message or "size" in message:
            status_code = 413
            audit["error_code"] = "PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE"
            raise UploadError("PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE", 413,
                              f"File exceeds the {CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES} byte limit.",
                              details={"max_bytes": CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES})
        status_code = 400
        audit["error_code"] = "MALFORMED_MULTIPART"
        raise UploadError("MALFORMED_MULTIPART", 400,
                          "Malformed multipart request body.")
    except OSError as exc:
        err = storage_error(exc, "request")
        outcome, status_code = "error", err.status_code
        audit["error_code"] = err.code
        raise err
    finally:
        # FM-100: exactly one audit record per attempt, ALWAYS — including paths
        # that raise. Success and failure are equally auditable.
        audit["outcome"] = outcome
        audit["status"] = status_code
        audit["duration_ms"] = round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000, 2)
        level = (logging.INFO if status_code < 400 or status_code == 499
                 else logging.WARNING if status_code < 500 else logging.ERROR)
        log_event(level, "upload.attempt", **audit)


async def _process_upload(request: Request, audit: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Parse the form, stream the part to disk, validate it, publish atomically."""

    # FM-06: bound the PARSER itself. max_files/max_fields stop a "multipart bomb"
    # — a body of 100k tiny parts that costs far more to parse than its byte count
    # suggests. max_part_size gives the parser its own ceiling on the file part.
    form_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {"max_files": CFG.MAX_FORM_FILES,
                                   "max_fields": CFG.MAX_FORM_FIELDS}
    try:
        form = await request.form(**form_kwargs,
                                  max_part_size=CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES + 1)
    except TypeError:
        # Older Starlette lacks max_part_size; the body-size middleware still caps.
        form = await request.form(**form_kwargs)

    try:
        # --- FM-07: the expected field must be present and must be a file -------
        files = [(k, v) for k, v in form.multi_items() if isinstance(v, UploadFile)]
        if not files:
            raise UploadError("MISSING_FILE", 400,
                              f"No file provided in field '{CFG.FILE_FIELD}'.",
                              details={"expected_field": CFG.FILE_FIELD})
        # FM-08: reject ambiguity rather than silently picking one.
        if len(files) > 1:
            raise UploadError("TOO_MANY_FILES", 400,
                              "Exactly one file may be uploaded per request.",
                              details={"received": len(files)})
        field_name, upload_file = files[0]
        if field_name != CFG.FILE_FIELD:
            raise UploadError("UNEXPECTED_FIELD", 400,
                              f"File must be sent in the '{CFG.FILE_FIELD}' field.",
                              details={"received_field": scrub(field_name, 64)})

        raw_name = upload_file.filename
        safe_name, name_flags = sanitize_filename(raw_name)
        audit["filename_raw"] = scrub(raw_name, 256)
        audit["filename_safe"] = safe_name
        audit["filename_flags"] = name_flags
        audit["declared_mime"] = scrub(upload_file.content_type, 128)

        check_free_space(CFG.MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES)

        stored, itype, meta = await _stream_validate_and_store(upload_file, audit)

        # FM-12: record when the client lied about the type. Not an error —
        # browsers send application/octet-stream routinely — but worth aggregating.
        declared_ext = extension_of(safe_name)
        audit["extension_mismatch"] = bool(
            declared_ext and _EXT_TO_TYPE.get(declared_ext) is not itype)
        audit["mime_mismatch"] = (upload_file.content_type or "").lower() \
            .split(";")[0].strip() != itype.mime

        return {
            "id": stored.sha256,
            "filename": safe_name,
            "original_filename": scrub(raw_name, 256),
            "stored_path": stored.relative_path,
            "url": f"/files/{stored.relative_path.replace(os.sep, '/')}",
            "mime_type": itype.mime,
            "size_bytes": stored.size,
            "sha256": stored.sha256,
            "width": meta.width,
            "height": meta.height,

        return self._fh.tell()

## Key design decisions worth calling out

**True streaming, not just "Flask parses it for me."** Instead of relying on `request.files` (which lets Werkzeug parse the whole multipart body before your view even runs), the handler calls `werkzeug.formparser.parse_form_data()` directly with a custom `stream_factory`. That factory hands back a `LimitedTempFileWriter` whose `.write()` is invoked by the parser once per chunk as bytes arrive off the socket. This gives three things at once: (1) the full body is never buffered in memory, (2) the size cap is enforced live, byte-by-byte, so a client that lies about — or omits — `Content-Length` still gets cut off at exactly `MAX_FILE_SIZE`, and (3) SHA-256 and the first-16-bytes magic header are computed for free during the same pass.

**Filename never touches the filesystem path.** `sanitize_filename()` produces a *display-only* name for logs/response. The actual on-disk name is always `uuid4().hex + <server-derived extension>`, so path traversal, null bytes, reserved device names, or overwrite attacks are structurally impossible regardless of sanitizer bugs.

**Type trust chain**: magic bytes (sniffed while streaming) → Pillow `verify()` → Pillow re-decode + `img.load()` to force full pixel decode → dimension/pixel-count cap. Client `Content-Type` and file extension are used only for logging, never for a trust decision.

**Atomicity**: write to a temp file in `.tmp/` on the *same filesystem* as the final directory (checked at startup via `st_dev`), `fsync` the file, `os.replace()` (atomic rename), then `fsync` the containing directory too, so a crash immediately after "success" can't leave a zero-length or missing file.

**Concurrency**: a bounded semaphore caps simultaneous uploads (→ 503 `SERVER_BUSY` when full) and a per-IP sliding-window rate limiter (→ 429 `RATE_LIMITED`) guards against a single client exhausting capacity. Both are called out as per-process only — multi-worker deployments need a shared backend (Redis) for real enforcement.

**Failure → HTTP/error-code map**:
| Code | HTTP | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | too many requests/IP/window |
| `SERVER_BUSY` | 503 | concurrency cap hit |
| `INVALID_CONTENT_TYPE` | 400 | not multipart/form-data |
| `INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE` | 507 | low/no disk space (pre-check, mid-write, or on rename) |
| `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Content-Length header or mid-stream cap exceeded |
| `MALFORMED_UPLOAD` | 400 | broken multipart body |
| `CLIENT_DISCONNECTED` | 400 | socket dropped mid-upload |
| `MISSING_FILE` / `TOO_MANY_FILES` / `INVALID_FILENAME` / `EMPTY_FILE` | 400 | field-level validation |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` / `INVALID_IMAGE` | 415 | magic-byte mismatch / failed decode / decompression bomb |
| `STORAGE_ERROR` | 500 | permission errors, unexpected OSError |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | anything unanticipated |
| success | 201 | with `Location` header + JSON metadata |

Every branch logs one structured JSON line via `log_attempt()`, and `cleanup_stale_temp_files()` reaps orphaned `.part` files left behind by crashes/restarts (call it from cron/APScheduler in production, not just at startup, since a `kill -9` can happen anytime).

One thing you'll need to adapt for real production use: the in-process semaphore/rate-limiter state and the startup-only cleanup are fine for a single-process dev/staging setup, but need Redis-backed equivalents and a periodic scheduler once you run multiple workers.

GENERIC_UPLOAD_MIMES = {"", "application/octet-stream"}
WINDOWS_RESERVED_NAMES = {
    "CON",
    "PRN",
    "AUX",
    "NUL",
    *(f"COM{i}" for i in range(1, 10)),
    *(f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1, 10)),
}

def log_event(event: str, **fields: object) -> None:
    """Emit machine-readable logs without interpolating untrusted strings."""

    record = {

        "timestamp": time.time(),
        **fields,
    }
    logger.info(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=True, default=str))

# Errors

class UploadError(Exception):
    def __init__(
        self,
        status: int,
        code: str,
        message: str,
        *,
        details: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.details = details or {}


def storage_error(exc: OSError) -> UploadError:
    """Convert internal OS errors without exposing filesystem paths."""

    if exc.errno in {errno.ENOSPC, getattr(errno, "EDQUOT", -1)}:
        return UploadError(
            500,
            "STORAGE_FULL",
            "The server does not have enough storage for this upload.",
        )

    if exc.errno in {errno.EACCES, errno.EPERM, errno.EROFS}:
        return UploadError(
            500,
            "STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE",
            "The upload storage is not writable.",
        )

    if exc.errno in {errno.EMFILE, errno.ENFILE}:
        return UploadError(
            500,
            "SERVER_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED",
            "The server temporarily lacks resources to process the upload.",
        )

    return UploadError(
        500,
        "STORAGE_IO_ERROR",
        "An I/O error occurred while storing the upload.",
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Secure storage setup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ensure_private_directory(path: Path, mode: int) -> None:
    """
    Create a directory and reject symlink/non-directory substitutions.

    The storage parent should also be controlled by the service account.
    """

    path.mkdir(parents=True, mode=mode, exist_ok=True)

    info = path.lstat()
    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        raise OSError(errno.ENOTDIR, "Storage path is not a real directory")

    # Staging and locks must not be accessible to other users.
    os.chmod(path, mode)


def ensure_storage() -> None:
    ensure_private_directory(UPLOAD_ROOT, 0o750)
    ensure_private_directory(STAGING_DIR, 0o700)
    ensure_private_directory(LOCK_DIR, 0o700)


def cleanup_stale_temporary_files() -> None:
    """
    Remove abandoned .part files left by crashes or forced restarts.

    Only regular files matching our private randomized naming convention are
    removed, and only after a long grace period.
    """

    cutoff = time.time() - STALE_TEMP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS

    try:
        for entry in STAGING_DIR.glob(".upload-*.part"):
            try:
                info = entry.lstat()
                if (
                    stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode)
                    and not stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode)
                    and info.st_mtime < cutoff
                ):
                    entry.unlink()
                    log_event("stale_upload_removed", name=entry.name)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
            except OSError as exc:
                log_event(
                    "stale_upload_cleanup_failed",
                    name=entry.name,
                    errno=exc.errno,
                )
    except OSError as exc:
        log_event("stale_upload_scan_failed", errno=exc.errno)

# Flask multipart streaming

class DiskStreamingRequest(FlaskRequest):
    """
    Force multipart file parts into private temporary files.

    Werkzeug otherwise keeps smaller uploads in a spooled in-memory object.
    This override ensures the parser never retains an entire uploaded file in
    application memory.
    """

    def _get_file_stream(
        self,
        total_content_length: int | None,
        content_type: str | None,
        filename: str | None = None,
        content_length: int | None = None,
    ) -> BinaryIO:
        ensure_storage()
        return tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode="w+b", dir=STAGING_DIR)


# In-process fallback for platforms without advisory file locking.
_local_upload_slots = threading.BoundedSemaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS)


@contextmanager
def acquire_upload_slot() -> Iterator[None]:
    """
    Bound simultaneous uploads.

    On Unix, lock files enforce the bound across multiple WSGI worker
    processes. On other platforms, a per-process semaphore is used.
    """

    if fcntl is None:
        acquired = _local_upload_slots.acquire(blocking=False)
        if not acquired:
            raise UploadError(
                503,
                "UPLOAD_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED",
                "The server is processing too many uploads. Try again later.",
            )

        try:
            yield
        finally:
            _local_upload_slots.release()
        return

    lock_fd: int | None = None

    try:
        for index in range(MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS):
            candidate_fd = os.open(
                LOCK_DIR / f"upload-{index}.lock",
                os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR,
                0o600,
            )

            try:
                fcntl.flock(candidate_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                lock_fd = candidate_fd
                break
            except BlockingIOError:
                os.close(candidate_fd)

        if lock_fd is None:
            raise UploadError(
                503,
                "UPLOAD_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED",
                "The server is processing too many uploads. Try again later.",
            )

        yield
    finally:
        if lock_fd is not None:
            try:
                fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            finally:
                os.close(lock_fd)

def sanitize_client_filename(raw_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """
    Validate and normalize an untrusted filename.

    Client filenames are never used as storage paths. This sanitization is for
    validation, logging, and display only.
    """

    if not raw_name:
        raise UploadError(400, "MISSING_FILENAME", "The file has no filename.")

    if len(raw_name) > 255 or len(raw_name.encode("utf-8", "ignore")) > 1024:
        raise UploadError(400, "INVALID_FILENAME", "The filename is too long.")

    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", raw_name)

    # Reject traversal instead of silently discarding path components.
    if "/" in normalized or "\\" in normalized:
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_FILENAME",
            "Path components are not allowed in filenames.",
        )

    # Reject NUL, control characters, bidi controls, and other invisible
    # Unicode formatting characters that can spoof extensions in interfaces.
    if any(unicodedata.category(char).startswith("C") for char in normalized):
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_FILENAME",
            "The filename contains unsafe characters.",
        )

    if normalized in {".", ".."} or normalized.startswith("."):
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_FILENAME",
            "Hidden or relative filenames are not allowed.",
        )

    if normalized.endswith((" ", ".")):
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_FILENAME",
            "The filename has an unsafe trailing character.",
        )

    extension = Path(normalized).suffix.removeprefix(".").lower() or None
    safe_name = secure_filename(normalized)

    if not safe_name:
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_FILENAME",
            "The filename becomes empty after sanitization.",
        )

    reserved_base = safe_name.split(".", 1)[0].upper()
    if reserved_base in WINDOWS_RESERVED_NAMES:
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_FILENAME",
            "The filename is reserved by an operating system.",
        )

    # Keep returned/logged values bounded. The stored name is generated by us.
    safe_name = safe_name[:180]
    return safe_name, extension


def detect_magic(prefix: bytes) -> str | None:
    """Identify formats from signatures, not extension or Content-Type."""

    if prefix.startswith(b"\xff\xd8\xff"):
        return "jpeg"

    if prefix.startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"):
        return "png"

    if prefix.startswith((b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a")):
        return "gif"

    if (
        len(prefix) >= 12
        and prefix[:4] == b"RIFF"
        and prefix[8:12] == b"WEBP"
    ):
        return "webp"

    return None


def validate_declared_metadata(
    detected_format: str,
    claimed_mime: str,
    filename_extension: str | None,
) -> None:
    """
    Reject obvious type spoofing while allowing absent/generic MIME headers.

    Magic bytes remain authoritative.
    """

    info = FORMAT_INFO[detected_format]

    if (
        claimed_mime not in GENERIC_UPLOAD_MIMES
        and claimed_mime not in info["claimed_mimes"]
    ):
        raise UploadError(
            415,
            "MIME_TYPE_MISMATCH",
            "The declared Content-Type does not match the file content.",
        )

    if (
        filename_extension is not None
        and filename_extension not in info["allowed_extensions"]
    ):
        raise UploadError(
            415,
            "FILE_EXTENSION_MISMATCH",
            "The filename extension does not match the file content.",
        )


def validate_container_ending(
    path: Path,
    detected_format: str,
    file_size: int,
) -> None:
    """
    Reject truncated containers and simple image-plus-payload polyglots.

    Pillow performs the deeper structural validation below.
    """

    with path.open("rb") as source:
        if detected_format == "jpeg":
            if file_size < 4:
                raise UploadError(400, "INVALID_IMAGE", "The JPEG is truncated.")
            source.seek(-2, os.SEEK_END)
            if source.read(2) != b"\xff\xd9":
                raise UploadError(
                    400,
                    "INVALID_IMAGE",
                    "The JPEG has no valid end marker.",
                )

        elif detected_format == "png":
            expected_end = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00IEND\xaeB`\x82"
            if file_size < len(expected_end):
                raise UploadError(400, "INVALID_IMAGE", "The PNG is truncated.")
            source.seek(-len(expected_end), os.SEEK_END)
            if source.read(len(expected_end)) != expected_end:
                raise UploadError(
                    400,
                    "INVALID_IMAGE",
                    "The PNG has an invalid ending or trailing data.",
                )

        elif detected_format == "gif":
            if file_size < 7:
                raise UploadError(400, "INVALID_IMAGE", "The GIF is truncated.")
            source.seek(-1, os.SEEK_END)
            if source.read(1) != b"\x3b":
                raise UploadError(
                    400,
                    "INVALID_IMAGE",
                    "The GIF has an invalid ending or trailing data.",
                )

        elif detected_format == "webp":
            source.seek(0)
            header = source.read(12)
            if len(header) != 12:
                raise UploadError(400, "INVALID_IMAGE", "The WebP is truncated.")

            declared_size = int.from_bytes(header[4:8], "little") + 8
            if declared_size != file_size:
                raise UploadError(
                    400,
                    "INVALID_IMAGE",
                    "The WebP container size is invalid.",
                )


def validate_decoded_image(path: Path, detected_format: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """
    Structurally verify and decode every frame.

    Decoding catches corrupt/truncated content that has valid magic bytes.
    Pixel, dimension, and frame limits mitigate decompression bombs.
    """

    if detected_format == "webp" and not features.check("webp"):
        raise UploadError(
            500,
            "IMAGE_DECODER_UNAVAILABLE",
            "The server is not configured with WebP support.",
        )

    expected_pillow_format = FORMAT_INFO[detected_format]["pillow_format"]

    try:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("error", Image.DecompressionBombWarning)

            # verify() performs format-specific structural and checksum checks.
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                if image.format != expected_pillow_format:
                    raise UploadError(
                        415,
                        "IMAGE_FORMAT_MISMATCH",
                        "The decoded image format does not match its signature.",
                    )

                width, height = image.size
                if width <= 0 or height <= 0:
                    raise UploadError(
                        400,
                        "INVALID_IMAGE_DIMENSIONS",
                        "The image dimensions are invalid.",
                    )

                if width > MAX_IMAGE_WIDTH or height > MAX_IMAGE_HEIGHT:
                    raise UploadError(
                        400,
                        "IMAGE_DIMENSIONS_EXCEEDED",
                        "The image dimensions are too large.",
                    )

                if width * height > MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS:
                    raise UploadError(
                        400,
                        "IMAGE_PIXEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
                        "The decoded image contains too many pixels.",
                    )

                image.verify()

            # verify() invalidates the decoder, so reopen and decode all frames.
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                frame_count = int(getattr(image, "n_frames", 1))

                if frame_count < 1 or frame_count > MAX_ANIMATION_FRAMES:
                    raise UploadError(
                        400,
                        "IMAGE_FRAME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
                        "The animation contains too many frames.",
                    )

                total_pixels = 0
                first_width, first_height = image.size

                for frame_index in range(frame_count):
                    image.seek(frame_index)
                    frame_width, frame_height = image.size

                    if (
                        frame_width <= 0
                        or frame_height <= 0
                        or frame_width > MAX_IMAGE_WIDTH
                        or frame_height > MAX_IMAGE_HEIGHT
                    ):
                        raise UploadError(
                            400,
                            "INVALID_IMAGE_DIMENSIONS",
                            "An image frame has invalid dimensions.",
                        )

                    total_pixels += frame_width * frame_height
                    if total_pixels > MAX_ANIMATION_TOTAL_PIXELS:
                        raise UploadError(
                            400,
                            "IMAGE_COMPLEXITY_EXCEEDED",
                            "The animation is too large when decoded.",
                        )

                    # Actually decode the frame to catch late/truncated data.
                    image.load()

                return first_width, first_height, frame_count

    except UploadError:
        raise
    except Image.DecompressionBombError as exc:
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "IMAGE_DECOMPRESSION_BOMB",
            "The image expands to an unsafe size.",
        ) from exc
    except Image.DecompressionBombWarning as exc:
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "IMAGE_DECOMPRESSION_BOMB",
            "The image expands to an unsafe size.",
        ) from exc
    except (
        UnidentifiedImageError,
        OSError,
        SyntaxError,
        ValueError,
        EOFError,
    ) as exc:
        raise UploadError(
            400,
            "INVALID_IMAGE",
            "The uploaded file is corrupt or is not a valid supported image.",
        ) from exc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Streaming and atomic storage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def write_all(destination: BinaryIO, data: bytes) -> None:
    """Handle short writes instead of assuming one write writes everything."""

    remaining = memoryview(data)
    while remaining:
        written = destination.write(remaining)
        if written is None or written <= 0:
            raise OSError(errno.EIO, "Short write while storing upload")
        remaining = remaining[written:]


def reserve_file_space(fd: int) -> None:
    """
    Reserve the maximum file size up front when supported.

    This reduces the chance of running out of disk space halfway through a
    write. The file is truncated to its actual size afterward.
    """

    if not hasattr(os, "posix_fallocate"):
        return

    try:
        os.posix_fallocate(fd, 0, MAX_FILE_BYTES)
    except OSError as exc:
        unsupported = {
            errno.EINVAL,
            errno.ENOSYS,
            getattr(errno, "EOPNOTSUPP", -1),
            getattr(errno, "ENOTSUP", -1),
        }
        if exc.errno not in unsupported:
            raise


def fsync_directory(path: Path) -> None:
    """Persist a rename in filesystems that support directory fsync."""

    flags = os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", 0)
    directory_fd = os.open(path, flags)

    try:
        try:
            os.fsync(directory_fd)
        except OSError as exc:
            unsupported = {
                errno.EINVAL,
                getattr(errno, "ENOTSUP", -1),
                getattr(errno, "EOPNOTSUPP", -1),
            }
            if exc.errno not in unsupported:
                raise
            log_event("directory_fsync_unsupported", errno=exc.errno)
    finally:
        os.close(directory_fd)


def store_upload_atomically(
    source: BinaryIO,
    claimed_mime: str,
    filename_extension: str | None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """
    Stream to a private temporary file, validate it, then atomically rename it.

    The temporary file and destination are on the same filesystem.
    """

    temp_path: Path | None = None
    published_path: Path | None = None
    fd = -1

    try:
        try:
            disk = shutil.disk_usage(STAGING_DIR)
            if disk.free < MAX_FILE_BYTES + MIN_FREE_DISK_RESERVE:
                raise UploadError(
                    500,
                    "STORAGE_CAPACITY_LOW",
                    "The server does not have enough free storage.",
                )

            fd, raw_temp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                prefix=".upload-",
                suffix=".part",
                dir=STAGING_DIR,
            )
            temp_path = Path(raw_temp_path)
            os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)
            reserve_file_space(fd)
        except UploadError:
            raise
        except OSError as exc:
            raise storage_error(exc) from exc

        byte_count = 0
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        prefix = bytearray()
        detected_format: str | None = None

        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb", buffering=0) as destination:
                fd = -1

                while True:
                    try:
                        chunk = source.read(CHUNK_SIZE)
                    except ClientDisconnected as exc:
                        raise UploadError(
                            400,
                            "UPLOAD_INTERRUPTED",
                            "The client disconnected before the upload completed.",
                        ) from exc
                    except OSError as exc:
                        raise UploadError(
                            500,
                            "UPLOAD_STREAM_READ_FAILED",
                            "The server could not read the uploaded stream.",
                        ) from exc

                    if not chunk:
                        break

                    if not isinstance(chunk, bytes):
                        raise UploadError(
                            400,
                            "INVALID_UPLOAD_STREAM",
                            "The upload stream returned invalid data.",
                        )

                    new_size = byte_count + len(chunk)
                    if new_size > MAX_FILE_BYTES:
                        raise UploadError(
                            413,
                            "FILE_TOO_LARGE",
                            "The uploaded file exceeds the 10 MiB limit.",
                            details={"max_bytes": MAX_FILE_BYTES},
                        )

                    if len(prefix) < 16:
                        required = 16 - len(prefix)
                        prefix.extend(chunk[:required])

                    if detected_format is None and len(prefix) >= 12:
                        detected_format = detect_magic(bytes(prefix))
                        if detected_format is None and len(prefix) >= 16:
                            raise UploadError(
                                415,
                                "UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE",
                                "Only JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP images are accepted.",
                            )

                        if detected_format is not None:
                            validate_declared_metadata(
                                detected_format,
                                claimed_mime,
                                filename_extension,
                            )

                    digest.update(chunk)

                    try:
                        write_all(destination, chunk)
                    except OSError as exc:
                        raise storage_error(exc) from exc

                    byte_count = new_size

                if byte_count == 0:
                    raise UploadError(
                        400,
                        "EMPTY_FILE",
                        "The uploaded file is empty.",
                    )

                if detected_format is None:
                    detected_format = detect_magic(bytes(prefix))

                if detected_format is None:
                    raise UploadError(
                        415,
                        "UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE",
                        "Only JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP images are accepted.",
                    )

                validate_declared_metadata(
                    detected_format,
                    claimed_mime,
                    filename_extension,
                )

                # posix_fallocate may have extended the file to 10 MiB.
                os.ftruncate(destination.fileno(), byte_count)

                # Persist all file data before validation/publication.
                os.fsync(destination.fileno())

        except UploadError:
            raise
        except OSError as exc:
            raise storage_error(exc) from exc

        assert temp_path is not None
        assert detected_format is not None

        validate_container_ending(temp_path, detected_format, byte_count)
        width, height, frame_count = validate_decoded_image(
            temp_path,
            detected_format,
        )

        info = FORMAT_INFO[detected_format]

        # A 256-bit random ID makes collision/overwrite risk negligible.
        upload_id = secrets.token_hex(32)
        stored_name = f"{upload_id}.{info['extension']}"
        published_path = UPLOAD_ROOT / stored_name

        # Defense in depth: never intentionally overwrite an existing object.
        if published_path.exists():
            raise UploadError(
                500,
                "STORAGE_NAME_COLLISION",
                "The server could not allocate a unique storage name.",
            )

        try:
            # Same-filesystem rename: readers see either no file or the complete,
            # validated file, never a partially written upload.
            os.replace(temp_path, published_path)
            temp_path = None
            os.chmod(published_path, 0o640)
            fsync_directory(UPLOAD_ROOT)
        except OSError as exc:
            # If durability failed after rename, remove the uncertain result.
            if published_path.exists():
                try:
                    published_path.unlink()
                    fsync_directory(UPLOAD_ROOT)
                except OSError as cleanup_exc:
                    log_event(
                        "published_upload_cleanup_failed",
                        name=published_path.name,
                        errno=cleanup_exc.errno,
                    )
            raise storage_error(exc) from exc

        return {
            "id": upload_id,
            "stored_name": stored_name,
            "content_type": info["mime"],
            "size": byte_count,
            "sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
            "width": width,
            "height": height,
            "frames": frame_count,
        }

    finally:
        if fd >= 0:
            try:
                os.close(fd)
            except OSError:
                pass

        # Covers validation failures, interrupted writes, short writes, disk-full
        # errors, exceptions, and normal application errors before publication.
        if temp_path is not None:
            try:
                temp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            except OSError as exc:
                log_event(
                    "temporary_upload_cleanup_failed",
                    name=temp_path.name,
                    errno=exc.errno,
                )

def create_app() -> Flask:
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.request_class = DiskStreamingRequest

    # Werkzeug rejects oversized bodies while parsing, including chunked bodies
    # when the WSGI server supplies a terminated input stream.
    app.config.update(
        MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH=MAX_REQUEST_BYTES,
        MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE=MAX_FORM_MEMORY_BYTES,
        MAX_FORM_PARTS=MAX_MULTIPART_PARTS,
    )

    ensure_storage()
    cleanup_stale_temporary_files()

    @app.before_request
    def begin_upload_log() -> None:
        if request.path != "/api/upload":
            return

        g.request_id = secrets.token_hex(16)
        g.upload_started = time.monotonic()
        g.upload_result_code = None
        g.upload_log_finished = False

        log_event(
            "upload_attempt_started",
            request_id=g.request_id,
            method=request.method,
            remote_address=request.remote_addr,
            content_length=request.content_length,
            content_type=request.content_type,
        )

    @app.after_request
    def finish_upload_log(response):
        if request.path != "/api/upload":
            return response

        response.headers["X-Request-ID"] = getattr(g, "request_id", "")
        response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
        response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"

        payload = response.get_json(silent=True) or {}
        error = payload.get("error") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
        error_code = error.get("code") if isinstance(error, dict) else None

        log_event(
            "upload_attempt_finished",
            request_id=getattr(g, "request_id", None),
            http_status=response.status_code,
            result_code=error_code or getattr(g, "upload_result_code", None),
            duration_ms=round(
                (time.monotonic() - getattr(g, "upload_started", time.monotonic()))
                * 1000,
                2,
            ),
            size=getattr(g, "uploaded_size", None),
            stored_name=getattr(g, "stored_name", None),
        )
        g.upload_log_finished = True
        return response

    @app.teardown_request
    def log_aborted_request(exception: BaseException | None) -> None:
        # Captures exceptional teardown paths where no response was produced.
        if (
            request.path == "/api/upload"
            and not getattr(g, "upload_log_finished", False)
        ):
            log_event(
                "upload_attempt_aborted",
                request_id=getattr(g, "request_id", None),
                exception_type=type(exception).__name__ if exception else None,
